issues.legal_issue: A recital in a registered gift deed that possession was handed to and accepted by the donee, considered with the circumstances of the transaction, can establish acceptance unless the donor affirmatively rebuts it.
material_facts: The donors executed registered deeds of gift in favour of their son, and the deeds recited that possession was handed over and accepted.
The gifts were made out of love and affection and were not onerous on their face.
The lower courts relied on the donee’s lack of tax payments, mutation, and overt acts of possession to find that he had not accepted the gifts.
The donors did not establish that the recitals were untrue or that the gifts were not voluntarily made; the donee had been living abroad.
issues.conclusion: Acceptance was established. The recitals and the circumstances raised a rebuttable presumption, and the burden lay on the donors to prove otherwise; the cited circumstances alone did not rebut it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 122 and 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, acceptance is essential to a valid gift, but no particular mode of acceptance is prescribed. Acceptance is determined from the circumstances; delivery of possession raises a presumption of acceptance, and express acceptance or an overt act is unnecessary. A recital in a registered deed that possession was delivered is an admission that raises a rebuttable presumption, placing the burden on the party alleging the contrary. The Court relied on Sanjukta Ray v. Bimelendu Mohanty, Kamakshi Ammal v. Rajalakshmi, Samrathi Devi v. Parsuram Pandey, Narayani Bhanumathi v. Karthyayani Lelitha Bhai, Prem Singh v. Birbal, and Alavi v. Aminakutty.

rule.if: gift_dispute_proceeding and registered_gift_deed and deed_recites_delivery_and_acceptance and non_onerous_gift and donors_failed_to_rebut_recitals

predicates.gift_dispute_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether a gift of property was validly accepted by the donee.
predicates.registered_gift_deed: The donor executed a registered deed transferring the property as a gift.
predicates.deed_recites_delivery_and_acceptance: The deed states that the donor delivered possession to the donee and that the donee accepted it.
predicates.non_onerous_gift: The gift is not made subject to an obligation that makes it onerous.
predicates.donors_failed_to_rebut_recitals: The donors did not affirmatively prove that possession was not delivered or that the deed’s recital was untrue.

issues.definition: When a property-gift dispute involves a registered deed reciting delivery and acceptance, the gift is treated as accepted if it is non-onerous and the donors fail to rebut the recital.

issues.legal_issue: A donor cannot turn a gift stated to be made out of love and affection into an onerous gift merely by alleging an external promise by the donee, absent proof of undue influence.
material_facts: The gift deeds stated that the property was given out of love and affection and to enable the donee to lead a good family life.
The donors alleged that the donee had promised to contribute money at his sister’s marriage and later failed to do so.
The deeds did not make that alleged contribution a condition of the gifts.
issues.conclusion: The alleged promise did not make the gifts onerous or justify treating them as conditional.
issues.legal_principle: Section 91 of the Indian Evidence Act applies to grants and other dispositions of property; the Court held that the distinction between a recital and a contractual term did not arise on these deed terms. Sections 91 and 92 govern proof contrary to written dispositions, subject to their exceptions. The Court distinguished Gangabai v. Chhabubai and Tyagaraja Mudaliyar v. Vedathanni because those cases concerned the nature of the transaction or document. To bring the case within Section 16 of the Indian Contract Act, undue influence had to be proved; it was not.

rule.if: gift_dispute_proceeding and deed_states_gift_is_out_of_affection and donor_alleges_unwritten_donee_promise and undue_influence_not_proved

predicates.gift_dispute_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether a property gift is valid or subject to an alleged obligation.
predicates.deed_states_gift_is_out_of_affection: The written gift deed states that the transfer is made out of love or affection rather than in exchange for a condition.
predicates.donor_alleges_unwritten_donee_promise: The donor alleges that the donee made a promise that is not stated as a condition in the deed.
predicates.undue_influence_not_proved: The donor did not prove that the deed was procured through undue influence.

issues.definition: If a deed describes an affectionate gift and the donor relies on an unwritten promise without proving undue influence, that alleged promise does not make the gift onerous.

issues.legal_issue: A completed valid gift cannot be rescinded because of the donee’s subsequent conduct or failure to perform an alleged obligation.
material_facts: The donors executed deeds of gift and later executed cancellation documents.
They based cancellation on the donee’s alleged failure to contribute money at his sister’s marriage.
The gifts were found to be valid and the alleged obligation was not a condition stated in the deeds.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation of the completed gifts was ineffective, and the trial court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Once a gift is complete, it cannot be rescinded for any reason based on the donee’s subsequent conduct. The Court applied this principle after finding the gifts valid and rejected the alleged obligation as a basis for cancellation.

predicates.gift_dispute_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the validity of a gift and a later attempt to cancel it.
predicates.valid_gift_completed: The gift was validly accepted and the transfer was complete.
predicates.donor_cancels_because_of_donee_subsequen: The donor attempts to cancel the completed gift because of conduct or an alleged failure by the donee after the gift.

issues.definition: When a valid gift is complete, a donor’s later cancellation based on the donee’s subsequent conduct is ineffective.
